writeup: TIC 72721266 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.5806 days, detected through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a dimming of 3.67 percent, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The signal achieves a detection significance of 76.9 in the Box Least Squares search, with pixel-level analysis yielding a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 10.9 and a centroid offset of 0.8 arcsec from the target position. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel find. The automated machine learning screening assigned this candidate a score of 0.35, indicating moderate confidence that this represents a real eclipsing system rather than a false positive.
